value: Official 1% acceptance compares sampled 0.4 |F| delta with initial sphere kinetic energy at 21.38 us. Separate 1% peak-overlap, peak-force and full-trace total-energy checks are supplemental. The 30.38 us endpoint is separated; rebound speed ratio is a diagnostic, not an official assertion.
LAMMPS wall material mixing uses E/[2(1-nu^2)]. Identical finite E=100 GPa and nu=0.25 on the FunDEM sphere and fixed plane match that exact effective modulus.
The wall is fixed in motion but its elastic modulus is finite. An infinite-modulus-wall conversion would double the intended effective modulus.
Effective contact mass is the full sphere mass; effective radius is the full sphere radius. Only the moving sphere contributes kinetic energy.
Restitution one gives exactly zero automatic damping. Tangential friction is zero and all tangential histories, force, torque and spin stay zero.
Wall contact impulse equals the sphere momentum change. The sphere alone is subject to external wall force and is not an isolated momentum-conserving system.
No coefficient fitting, solver source changes or local LAMMPS executable rerun. Reference states come from pinned official YAML.
Native historical native application build CPU/CUDA libraries are tested; installed GUI executable byte identity is not established.
Every integration step, including the initial frame, is retained in native binary result and CSV.
YAML epsilon=1e-10 is same-code regression precision; it does not replace the official 1% analytic criterion.
